The body after the tall looped f has a closed oval head and a long descending stroke returning into an enclosed lower loop. This matches the closed returning lower stroke on the PDF204 q in t4q and the local q at end of L06; the PDF g in g6 has a shorter open hooked tail. The lower loop is visible as part of the whole glyph, not inferred from a Czech word.

The first interior digit of n383 has two right-facing curved lobes. It lacks the angular open top, upright and horizontal junction of the clear 4 signs elsewhere on this same card. Both the complete group and the native context show a 3-shaped body.

The second body of 3ht8g586 has a low right shoulder and a downstroke extending below the baseline; it lacks the tall closed ascender loop present in PDF h (e.g. th6r1) and in the h in L06 d3h3d3. Its low shoulder and descender are closer to PDF p in 6p1. The p/r boundary is less decisive than the exclusion of tall-loop h.

The fourth body has two closed lobes with a central waist, like the other 8 signs on the card. A tall h would have an open right shoulder attached to an ascender loop, not the two-lobed figure present here.

The fifth body has a rounded head and an open lower hook returning leftward without an enclosed lower loop. It matches the open-tailed g in PDF g6, contrasting with the closed lower loop on the disputed L03 q.

The third body is a short open curved c. It has no tall upright or crossing bar; the immediately following d-like body does have a tall looped/crossed stroke. PDF t and d examples both preserve more stem structure than the third body has.

The sixth body is a low shoulder rising from the baseline, with a short left stem and right exit. It resembles the short r in the PDF t832r1ř group. The clear 7 signs on 253 (for example L02 first body and L07 after m5) have a long slanting descending stroke and a separate crossbar. Those features are absent here. A tall h ascender loop is also absent.

The third body of d3h3d3 has an elongated closed ascender loop followed by a low right shoulder. This matches PDF h and contrasts with its low shoulder r. The ascending loop is visible and is not a detached mark.

The first body has two low humps rather than one; the second has a flat upper stroke and lower bowl matching 5, not the two curved lobes of 3. A visible gap separates this pair from the following crossed descending 7 and 5. The bodies can be compared with m in nm5 on L01 and 5/7 elsewhere on the same card.

editorial_czech.text: Proč na mne úplně zapomínáš, Aničko moje jediná? Již čtrnácté dnů je tomu, co jsem od tebe nedostal ani slůvka. Jsi snad churava? Či nejsem již tvým Pepoušem a nejsi ty již mou tak vřele [milovanou?] Anduličkou? [Obdržela?] jsi můj lístek ze dne šestého [tohoto?] měsíce? Prosím aspoň o několik slov. Srdéčko [moje je?] velice smutné a neklidné. Tisíc vřelých, upřímných pus ti posílá zarmoucený Pepouš.
